english.title: False unsworn evidence at an inquest by a person aged 14 years or over
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person aged 14 years or over, appeared as a witness at an inquest at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..) into **(..SPECIFY THE CIRCUMSTANCES REQUIRING THE INQUEST..) and gave unsworn evidence which was false in that **(..SPECIFY THE FALSE NATURE OF THE EVIDENCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 8(1) and (2) of Schedule 6 to the Coroners and Justice Act 2009.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: (i) Paragraph 8(4) of Schedule 6 to the Coroners and Justice Act 2009 provides that for the purposes of paragraph 8(3), a person's age is to be taken to be that which it appears to the court to be after considering any available evidence.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 51 weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding not exceeding £1000.

In relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 a reference in this Schedule to 51 weeks is to be read as a reference to 6 months, paragraph 10 of Schedule 6 to the Coroners and Justice Act 2009.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months
